issues.description: The template's Bitmap24 class header declares a three-parameter constructor (Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth)) while the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) defines a two-parameter constructor (Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height)). The solution repository uses the two-parameter constructor. This mismatch in the template will confuse students and can cause compilation or linkage issues when using the class or following the solution design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template header match the implementation and the solution: change the Bitmap24 constructor declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height); (remove the unused 'depth' parameter) or update the .cpp to provide a matching three-parameter constructor if that was intended. Prefer matching the solution's two-parameter signature to avoid confusing students.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor signature is inconsistent between the template header and the implementation/solution. The template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) (three parameters), but the template implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) (two parameters). The solution repository's header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) also declares the two-argument constructor. This mismatch creates a mapping/confusion problem for students (and may cause compilation/link issues) because the header in the template does not match the implementation or the intended solution API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template header with the implementation and solution by changing the template header declaration to Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height); OR update the implementation (and solution) to provide a matching three-argument constructor if the depth parameter is required. Preferably, remove the unused 'depth' parameter from the header to match the existing implementation and the solution.
